decks.title: Issue of Debentures — Part 1: Issue for Cash, Terms of Redemption and Capital Losses
goals: State the Companies Act, 2013 rules that shape an issue of debentures
Pass entries for debentures issued at par, at a premium or at a discount, in a lump sum or in instalments, with refunds
Record the six combinations of issue and redemption terms, with Discount or Loss on Issue of Debentures
Write off capital losses in the year they arise, in the ISC order

slides.heading: Issue of Debentures
slides.body_md: Part 1 — the **law**, issue **for cash**, the six **issue-redemption terms** and writing off **capital losses**. Every company, person and figure in this chapter is imagined.

nodes.label: Issue for cash: lump sum or instalments

visual.alt: Route map of Part 1: debentures under the Companies Act two thousand thirteen, issue for cash in a lump sum or instalments, issue at par, premium or discount, the six combinations of issue and redemption terms, and writing off capital losses
visual.caption: Part 1 at a glance

slides.narration: A company that needs long-term money without adding new owners can borrow it from the public by issuing debentures. In this part we look at the rules of the Companies Act, record debentures issued for cash at par, at a premium or at a discount, add the terms on which they will be repaid, and learn how the syllabus wants capital losses written off.

slides.heading: What the Companies Act, 2013 says
bullets: A debentureholder is a **creditor**, never a member.
Debentures may be issued at a **discount**; shares may not.

rows: Section 2(30): an instrument of debt, secured or not; the holder is a **creditor**
Section 71: debentures cannot carry voting rights
Allowed for debentures; barred for shares by Section 53 (sweat equity apart)
Credited to Securities Premium; Section 52 lists its uses, incl. writing off discount on debentures
Interest at the coupon rate on face value: a charge against profit

visual.alt: Table of points from the Companies Act two thousand thirteen: a debenture is an instrument of debt and its holder a creditor; debentures carry no voting rights; debentures may be issued at a discount though shares may not; premium is credited to securities premium whose uses include writing off discount on debentures; interest is a charge against profit

slides.narration: Under the Companies Act, a debenture is an instrument of debt, so its holder is a creditor of the company. Debentures cannot carry voting rights. Unlike shares, they may be issued below face value. Any premium received goes to securities premium, which the Act allows to be used for writing off a discount on debentures. Interest is paid at a fixed rate on the face value.

slides.heading: Issuing debentures for cash
slides.body_md: However the money is collected, the **Debentures Account is credited with face value**.

nodes.label: Lump sum: whole price with the application
Debentures Account always credited at face value

visual.alt: Flow of ways to issue debentures for cash: in a lump sum with the application, or in instalments on application, allotment and calls; excess application money is refunded; the debentures account is always credited at face value
visual.caption: Issue for cash

slides.narration: Debentures may be paid for in one lump sum with the application, or in instalments on application, allotment and one or more calls. If more debentures are applied for than are offered, the extra application money is refunded. Whatever the price and however it is collected, the debentures account always shows the face value, the amount the company owes.

slides.narration: In an issue by instalments, every stage is made due first and then received. Application money is transferred to the debentures account once allotment is made, and any excess is refunded. Allotment carries any premium, and any discount or loss on issue is recorded there too. The final call completes the face value.

slides.heading: Terms of redemption: six combinations
slides.body_md: A **premium on redemption** is promised now, so it is a loss now and a liability until repaid.

rows: Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr.
Loss on Issue Dr.; Premium on Redemption Cr.
Loss on Issue Dr. (discount + redemption premium); Premium on Redemption Cr.
Securities Premium Cr.; Loss on Issue Dr.; Premium on Redemption Cr.

visual.alt: Table of the six combinations of issue and redemption terms and the extra accounts in the allotment entry: none for par and par; discount on issue for a discount; securities premium for a premium; loss on issue and premium on redemption whenever the debentures are redeemable at a premium

slides.narration: When debentures are issued, the company also fixes how it will repay them, at par or at a premium. That gives six combinations. A premium on issue is credited to securities premium. A discount alone is debited to discount on issue. Whenever repayment is at a premium, the promised premium is credited to a liability account and, together with any discount, debited to loss on issue.

slides.body_md: 2,000 9% debentures of ₹100 each under each set of terms (allotment entry amounts).

visual.caption: Every row satisfies: cash + discount or loss = face value + securities premium + premium on redemption.

slides.narration: Here are the six combinations for two thousand debentures. The debentures account is credited with the same face value every time. What changes is the cash, the premium credited, the redemption premium promised and the loss debited. In every row, cash plus loss equals face value plus both premiums, a handy check.

slides.heading: Writing off capital losses: the ISC rule
bullets: Write off **in the year** the loss arises.
Order: **Securities Premium** → **Statement of Profit and Loss** → **Capital Reserve**.

nodes.label: Capital loss of the year (discount, loss on issue)

visual.alt: Flow of the ISC order for writing off a capital loss in the year it arises: first securities premium, then the statement of profit and loss, and lastly capital reserve
visual.caption: ISC 2027 note: written off in the year of the loss, in this order

slides.narration: Discount and loss on issue are capital losses. The syllabus says every capital loss must be written off in the year in which it occurs, not spread over the life of the debentures. Use securities premium first, then the statement of profit and loss, and capital reserve only as the last resort.

slides.body_md: At 31 March 2026 the loss of ₹75,000 is written off. The only securities premium is the ₹60,000 from worked example 2.

slides.narration: To sum up: debentures are always credited at face value. A premium on issue goes to securities premium, a discount to discount on issue, and any premium on redemption creates a loss on issue and a liability. Extra application money is refunded. Capital losses are written off in the year they arise, from securities premium, then profit and loss, then capital reserve.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: Credit the Debentures Account with **face value** in every entry; premium and discount go to their own accounts.
If redemption is at a **premium**, debit **Loss on Issue** (not Discount on Issue) and credit **Premium on Redemption**.
Check each allotment entry: **cash + loss = face value + premiums**.
Write off the loss in the **same year**, and show the **order** (Securities Premium first) in your working.
Name the stage in each narration (application, allotment, call, refund): it earns the step mark.
slides.narration: A few habits save marks. Always credit the debentures account at face value and send premium and discount to their own accounts. When repayment is at a premium, use loss on issue and credit premium on redemption. Check every allotment entry with the identity. Write off the loss in the same year and show the order. And label each entry with its stage.

slides.heading: Debentures other than for cash, interest and disclosure
slides.body_md: Part 2 — **promoters, underwriters and vendors**, **collateral security**, **calls in arrears and in advance**, **interest with TDS** and the **Balance Sheet**.

nodes.label: Calls in arrears and in advance

visual.alt: Route map of Part 2: debentures to promoters, underwriters and vendors, debentures as collateral security, calls in arrears and in advance, interest with tax deducted at source, and disclosure in the balance sheet
visual.caption: Part 2 at a glance

slides.narration: Not every debenture is sold for cash. Companies pay promoters, underwriters and sellers of assets with debentures, and pledge debentures to banks as security. Instalments may be paid late or early. Interest must be paid with tax deducted at source. Finally, all of it must be shown correctly in the balance sheet. Our running company is Kalsubai Hydraulic Jacks of Akole.

slides.heading: Debentures for consideration other than cash
slides.body_md: The vendor is first **credited** with the price; the debentures then **settle** that credit.

visual.alt: Table of entries for debentures issued for consideration other than cash: to promoters through incorporation costs or goodwill; to underwriters through underwriting commission; to vendors of assets or a business through the vendor account, with goodwill or capital reserve; the number of debentures is the amount payable divided by the issue price

slides.narration: When debentures settle a claim instead of bringing in cash, debit what the company received. Promoters are paid for forming the company, so incorporation costs, or goodwill, is debited. Underwriters earn a commission. A vendor is first credited with the price of the asset or business, and the debentures then settle that amount. Divide the amount payable by the issue price to find how many debentures to issue.

notes.title: Issue of Debentures — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Debentures, the Companies Act, 2013 and issue for cash
sections.body_md:
A **debenture** is an instrument of debt issued by a company under its common seal or otherwise (Section 2(30) of the **Companies Act, 2013**); the holder is a **creditor** who earns interest at a fixed (coupon) rate on the face value. Debentures carry **no voting rights** (Section 71). Unlike shares (Section 53), debentures **may be issued at a discount**.

**Issue for cash**
- **Lump sum:** Bank A/c Dr. To Debenture Application and Allotment A/c (all applications); on allotment that account is debited and the Debentures A/c credited.
- **Instalments:** application, allotment and one or more calls; each is first made due and then received.
- **Over-subscription:** the excess application money is refunded (Debenture Application A/c Dr. To Bank A/c).

Redemption of debentures (Debenture Redemption Reserve, investment, methods) is chapter 8; here redemption appears only as a **term of issue**.

key_terms.definition_md: An instrument acknowledging a debt of the company, carrying interest at a fixed rate on its face value; the holder is a creditor.
The rate of interest written on the debenture, applied to its face value.
Applications for more debentures than are offered; the extra application money is refunded.

rows: Section 2(30): an instrument of debt, secured or not; the holder is a **creditor**
Section 71: debentures cannot carry voting rights
Allowed for debentures; barred for shares by Section 53 (sweat equity apart)
Credited to Securities Premium; Section 52 lists its uses, incl. writing off discount on debentures
Interest at the coupon rate on face value: a charge against profit

sections.heading: 3. Terms of redemption: the six combinations and the loss on issue
sections.body_md:
At issue the company also fixes whether it will repay at **par** or at a **premium**.

- Redeemable at par: only the issue terms matter (par, premium, discount).
- Redeemable at a premium: **Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr.** with (discount, if any + premium on redemption); **Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c Cr.** with the premium payable.

**Identity (every allotment entry):** amount receivable + discount or loss = face value + securities premium + premium on redemption.

**Premium on Redemption of Debentures** is a **liability** until redemption, shown under other long-term liabilities.

key_terms.definition_md: The extra amount, above face value, that the company promises to pay when it repays the debentures.
The discount on issue plus any premium payable on redemption, recognised at the time of issue.

sections.heading: 6. Debentures issued as collateral security
sections.body_md:
**Collateral security** is a secondary security given in addition to the primary security for a loan. The lender can enforce the debentures only if the company fails to repay the loan; on repayment they are returned.

- **First method:** no entry. Below the loan in the note: *(secured by the issue of … debentures as collateral security)*.
- **Second method:** Debenture Suspense A/c Dr. To Debentures A/c (face value). In the note on long-term borrowings, the debentures are shown **less Debenture Suspense**, so they add nothing to the total. On repayment of the loan the entry is reversed.
- **No interest** is paid on collateral debentures; interest is paid on the loan.

key_terms.definition_md: An additional security pledged with a lender, enforceable only if the borrower defaults.
The account debited when collateral debentures are recorded by the second method; deducted from those debentures in the Balance Sheet.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Crediting the Debentures Account with the issue price instead of the face value.
- Debiting Discount on Issue when redemption is at a premium (use **Loss on Issue**), or forgetting the **Premium on Redemption** liability.
- Spreading the loss on issue over several years; the ISC note requires it to be written off in the **year of issue**, Securities Premium first.
- Dividing by the face value instead of the **issue price** to find debentures for a vendor.
- Paying or charging interest on **collateral debentures**.
- Debiting Debenture Interest with the net amount; it carries the **gross** interest.
- Leaving debentures due within twelve months under long-term borrowings.

**How marks are usually awarded (SOYL chapter tests on the ISC default pattern)**
- 1 mark: objective items.
- 2 marks: two or three journal entries, a distinction or a short disclosure.
- 3 marks: a set of entries for one issue (application to call), a write-off with its working, or a note to accounts.
- 5 marks in parts, e.g. (a) 3 + (b) 2: entries for an issue and a write-off or a note.
- Full practical (practice, 8 marks): journal for the issue about 4, write-off about 2, Balance Sheet notes about 2. The ISC 2027 weightage for Issue and Redemption of Debentures in Paper I is 8 marks.

**Figures in SOYL practice** are imagined; your board paper will give its own.

questions.stem_md: Hampta Pass Battery Works Ltd, an imagined company at Naggar, has issued 9% debentures to the public. Under Section 71 of the Companies Act, 2013, the holders of these debentures

options.text_md: vote at general meetings in proportion to the face value of debentures they hold
cannot be given any voting rights at the general meetings of the company
become members of the company as soon as the debentures are allotted
share in the profits of the company along with its equity shareholders

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** cannot be given any voting rights at the general meetings of the company. Section 71 forbids a company to issue debentures that carry voting rights. A debentureholder has lent money to the company: he is its creditor, not a member.

questions.stem_md: The directors of Sela Pass Wind Turbines Ltd, an imagined company at Dirang, wish to raise long-term funds by issuing securities below their face value. Under the Companies Act, 2013, they may issue at a discount

both equity shares and debentures, once the debentureholders consent
neither equity shares nor debentures
debentures, but not equity shares (sweat equity shares apart)

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** debentures, but not equity shares (sweat equity shares apart). Section 53 bars the issue of shares at a discount, sweat equity apart. No such bar applies to debentures; the discount is a capital loss to be written off.
